subject: NeuraMed renewal: commit ladder proposal and sizing based on Q1-Q2 usage
messages:
From: Ally Chen <ally.chen@neuramed.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-20T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal planning — data and timing

Vanessa,

Hope you're well — our renewal is coming up in August and the finance team wants a clearer picture of capacity needs before we sign on another year. We saw a spike in March and again in May where peak concurrency hit ~120 v100-equivalent slots for short windows. Our infra team is worried about steadying unit costs while preserving latency for inference during peaks.

Can you share a proposal that ties the commit to our actual Q1–Q2 usage (not just historical peaks)? Ideally we'd like a laddered approach: baseline reserved capacity + on-demand burst credits. Also please include expected cost delta if we add a second pool of H100s versus staying on n1-standard GPU mix.

Thanks — copying procurement (procurement@neuramed.com) for timeline.

— Ally
Ally Chen
Head of AI Ops, NeuraMed
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Ally Chen <ally.chen@neuramed.com>, Rajiv Singh <rajiv.singh@neuramed.com>
Cc: procurement@neuramed.com
Date: 2027-06-21T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — data and timing

Ally / Rajiv / procurement team,

Thanks for the context — attached is a short read: (1) a usage export for Q1–Q2 2027 and (2) a first-pass commit ladder that maps baseline reserved GPUs to observed sustained usage and keeps a burst buffer for peaks. Highlights:

- Observed sustained average (rolling 7d) = ~42 H100-equivalent GPU-hours/day (normalized).
- Peak 99th percentile short windows reached ~115 H100-equivalent GPU-hours for 1–3 hour bursts.
- Proposed ladder: baseline reserve at 50 H100-equivalent, a mid-tier at +40, and a burst credit pool of 70 (convertible to on-demand at fixed uplift).
- Cost note: switching baseline to H100 reduces per-token latency by ~25% and improves throughput density; incremental monthly committed cost is ~17% higher vs current mixed fleet, but expected per-token cost falls by ~9% given improved packing.

What I'd like from you: confirm the expected cadence of the May/Mar style bursts (frequency/seasonality) and whether you want hard SLA-backed headroom or a more cost-flexible commit with burst credits. I'll loop in Karthik/Ben for pricing cadence and contract framing.

Attachments: NeuraMed_usage_report_Q1-Q2_2027.csv, proposed_commit_ladder_v1.xlsx

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0172
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-22T08:46:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal planning — data and timing (NeuraMed) — sizing ask

Karthik / Ben,

Forwarding NeuraMed's usage export and my first-pass ladder. Key asks from customer: tie commit to actual usage and give a laddered commit (baseline + mid + burst). They are open to H100 baseline but will weigh committed dollars vs unit cost improvements.

Can you: 1) run a pricing calc for the three-ladder model in the attached spreadsheet (baseline 50 H100-equivalent, mid +40, burst credits 70), 2) give two contract frames — a) 12mo commit with 3-month rolling topup option, b) 24mo discounted commit with automated usage reconciliation, and 3) recommend an SLA headroom threshold (we typically propose 20% headroom on baseline for enterprise deals).

I'd prefer a modest short-term incentive: a one-time onboarding credit if they sign by July 15. Also note procurement asked for PO timeline — they'd like the final SOW/price before July 5.

Thanks,
Vanessa
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-24T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal planning — sizing ask (NeuraMed)

Vanessa, Karthik — ran the numbers off the usage export and the ladder model. Quick summary (all monthly):

- Baseline 50 H100-equivalent reserve = $152k / month (committed rate), covers sustained demand and yields ~9% per-token reduction vs mixed fleet.
- Mid-tier +40 reserve = incremental $108k / month; recommended to be optional add-on that ramps at 60% utilization of baseline for 3 consecutive weeks.
- Burst credits 70 = pre-purchased credits at a 20% discount vs on-demand burst pricing; expected to cover two typical March/May style events per quarter.
- 12mo frame: effective blended discount ~11% vs on-demand. 24mo frame: additional 4% discount with a reconciliation clause (quarterly usage true-up with credits applied).
- SLA/Headroom: propose a 20% baseline headroom guarantee with a runbook for automatic routing to mid-tier or burst pool before fallbacks. For hard SLA-backed latency at 99th percentile during peaks, add an SLA uplift fee (we recommend passing that through to a premium mid-tier).

I'll draft two pricing lines for the SOW and a short explanation of how burst credits convert to on-demand at expiration. Recommend we offer onboarding credit equal to one week of baseline committed fees if they sign before July 15.

— Ben
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
From: Rajiv Singh <rajiv.singh@neuramed.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@neuramed.com, Ally Chen <ally.chen@neuramed.com>
Date: 2027-06-27T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — data and timing

Vanessa / Ben / Karthik,

Appreciate the fast turnaround and clear options. After internal review, NeuraMed is comfortable with the laddered approach: baseline 50 H100-equivalent reserve, opt into mid-tier +40 after usage hits the trigger, and pre-purchase 70 burst credits for the first 12 months. We prefer the 12-month frame with the onboarding credit and the quarterly reconciliation report.

Procurement has asked me to attach the signed MOU for internal tracking and to request the SOW + final quote so we can issue a PO. Timeline: we need the SOW and invoice by July 3 to route for the July 8 procurement meeting.

Attachments: signed_mou_neuramed.pdf

Next steps: can you provide the SOW and a single-line invoice for the first month (baseline prorated from Aug 1) and the burst credits charge? Also confirm whether the mid-tier ramp trigger is evaluated on a rolling 21-day basis or calendar weeks (we prefer rolling).

Thanks — looking forward to closing this.

Rajiv Singh
Head of Infrastructure, NeuraMed
procurement@neuramed.com
